title: Arginase deficiency: enzyme normally produces urea
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the office due to abnormal motor development. He was born at 40 weeks gestation and had an unremarkable perinatal course. The boy developed normally during the first year of life. However, for the past 2 years, he has had progressive bilateral leg stiffness and abnormal involuntary movements. His cognitive and motor development is also delayed. There is no significant family history of neurological or muscular disorders. The patient's height, weight, and head circumference are below the 3rd percentile. Examination shows bilateral spastic paresis of his lower extremities and frequent choreoathetoid movements. Comprehensive laboratory testing reveals significantly elevated arginine levels in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid. The deficient enzyme in this patient is normally involved in the production of which of the following?

clues.text: progressive bilateral leg stiffness and abnormal involuntary movements
clues.note: Progressive SPASTIC diplegia with choreoathetoid movements and developmental regression is the classic neurologic picture of arginase deficiency.

clues.text: significantly elevated arginine levels in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid
clues.note: Markedly elevated ARGININE points to a block at ARGINASE, the last urea cycle enzyme (which normally converts arginine to urea + ornithine).

whatMatters: Progressive spastic diplegia + choreoathetosis + growth delay + markedly ELEVATED ARGININE = ARGINASE DEFICIENCY (a urea cycle disorder). Arginase is the final urea-cycle enzyme; it normally converts arginine to ORNITHINE + UREA. So the deficient enzyme is normally involved in producing UREA. Answer F.
strategy: Localize the block from the accumulating substrate: elevated ARGININE = arginase deficiency (arginine is arginase's substrate). Recall arginase's product: it hydrolyzes arginine to ornithine + UREA (the final step of the urea cycle, disposing of ammonia nitrogen). So the enzyme normally makes urea. Reject the products of unrelated pathways: GABA (glutamate decarboxylase), glutamine (glutamine synthetase/ammonia transport), homocysteine (methionine metabolism), orotic acid (pyrimidine synthesis/other urea-cycle blocks), and serotonin (tryptophan).

eliminations.label: GABA - made by glutamate decarboxylase
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: gamma-aminobutyric acid, formed from glutamate by glutamate decarboxylase (needs vitamin B6). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's unrelated to arginine/the urea cycle. ✅ Correct if: an inhibitory neurotransmitter/glutamate decarboxylase question.

eliminations.label: Glutamine - made by glutamine synthetase
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glutamine, which carries ammonia from tissues to the kidney (made by glutamine synthetase). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's not the product of arginase. ✅ Correct if: ammonia transport/glutamine synthesis.

eliminations.label: Homocysteine - methionine metabolism
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: homocysteine, an intermediate of methionine/folate metabolism (raised in B6/B12/folate deficiency). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated to the urea cycle/arginine. ✅ Correct if: homocystinuria or atherosclerosis-related homocysteine questions.

eliminations.label: Orotic acid - pyrimidine synthesis / proximal urea-cycle blocks
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: orotic acid, a pyrimidine-synthesis intermediate; it accumulates when carbamoyl phosphate is diverted (as in ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: arginase deficiency does not primarily overproduce orotic acid, and arginase's product is urea. ✅ Correct if: OTC deficiency or hereditary orotic aciduria.

eliminations.label: Serotonin - from tryptophan
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: serotonin (5-HT), synthesized from tryptophan by hydroxylation/decarboxylation. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated to arginine or the urea cycle. ✅ Correct if: a serotonin/tryptophan metabolism question.

reasoning: Progressive spastic diplegia + choreoathetosis + growth delay with markedly elevated arginine
Elevated arginine indicates a block at ARGINASE (arginine is its substrate)
Arginase normally hydrolyzes arginine to ornithine + UREA (last urea cycle step)
-> the deficient enzyme normally produces urea; answer F
mechanism: The urea cycle detoxifies ammonia by converting it into urea for excretion. Its final enzyme, ARGINASE, hydrolyzes ARGININE into ORNITHINE (which re-enters the cycle) and UREA. In ARGINASE DEFICIENCY (an autosomal recessive urea cycle disorder), arginine cannot be cleaved, so it ACCUMULATES in plasma and CSF; the disease presents distinctively - unlike other urea cycle defects, it usually lacks severe neonatal hyperammonemia and instead causes a PROGRESSIVE, later-onset picture of SPASTIC DIPLEGIA, choreoathetoid movements, developmental regression, and growth failure. The key to the question: the DEFICIENT enzyme (arginase) is normally involved in producing UREA (and ornithine). Diagnosis rests on the elevated arginine; treatment is an arginine-free, low-protein diet. The distractors are products of unrelated pathways: GABA (glutamate decarboxylase), glutamine (glutamine synthetase), homocysteine (methionine/folate metabolism), orotic acid (pyrimidine synthesis; accumulates in ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency), and serotonin (tryptophan).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biochem > urea cycle: arginase converts arginine -> ornithine + urea (last step); arginase deficiency -> ↑arginine, progressive spastic diplegia (mild/no hyperammonemia); treat low-protein/arginine-free diet.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Elevated arginine = arginase deficiency; arginase's normal product is urea.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on arginase, urea cycle, arginine/ornithine, spastic diplegia, or orotic acid? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: GABA (glutamate decarboxylase), glutamine (synthetase), homocysteine (methionine), orotic acid (pyrimidine/OTC), serotonin (tryptophan) are other pathways.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: arginase deficiency = ↑arginine, spastic diplegia; arginase makes urea + ornithine (final urea cycle step).

keywords.front: Why arginase deficiency differs from other urea cycle defects
keywords.back: Progressive spastic diplegia, usually mild/no hyperammonemia
Pyrimidine synthesis; OTC deficiency (urea cycle) / orotic aciduria

memoryHook: Arginine piles up because arginase - the urea cycle's final scissors - is broken; its normal job is snipping arginine into ornithine and UREA.
